transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 PT / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Samir (CTO - Crestline), Evan (Head of Platform), Priya (SRE)

Summary: quick operational triage following last week's latency/regression spike that caused degraded throughput on their private deployment. Focus on immediate hotfix path, canary rollout, and long-term playbook updates. Some transcript noise and misrecognitions present.

Topics: incident timeline recap; suspected KV/prefix cache regression; memory pressure vs long-tail queueing; rollback vs rollforward tradeoffs; security/audit requests; scheduling canary and on-call coverage.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we'll try to keep this tight, 45 to 60 minutes, main goal is to hand off the hotfix plan and agree canary windows.
[00:12] Samir: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we were hit pretty hard last thursday 11:40 UTC; our dashboards showed the p95 jumping and then a pile up in the request queue.
[00:22] Evan: to add, tokens per request didn't change much, it's almost like an internal cache miss cascade, the kv cache stopped returning prefixes and everything degraded.
[00:35] Omar: ok, that's consistent with what the logs show — we see amortized token compute rising and some big spikes tied to a specific redis-like eviction path. might be an edge in the kv-cache codepath we introduced in the last release.
[00:48] Priya: just to be clear, we run Redwood Private in our VPC, dedicated pools; we pushed the 2026.12.09 rollout and that's when the error window starts.
[01:05] Maya: right — so two parallel tracks: immediate hotfix (rollforward) vs rollback to prior image, which works but loses some perf improvements. what are your risk tolerances?
[01:20] Samir: rollback is low risk short term but our ops can't afford repeated regressions. we'd prefer a tested rollforward that fixes the root cause.
[01:34] Omar: understood. we sketched a hotfix that adds stricter kv-cache size bounds and an early-evict heuristic; it prevents pathological cache growth and handles stale prefix entries. we also added telemetry to trace head/tail misses.
[01:48] Evan: telemetry would be great — can you show what traces you'll need from our side?
[02:00] Omar: yes — token-level request traces covering 11:30 to 12:15 UTC, the flamegraphs, and heap snapshots if possible. we'll correlate with our trace ids.
[02:12] Priya: small note — our security team will need the audit trail for the patch. SOC2 and KMS info are required before we apply anything to prod.
[02:24] Maya: absolutely, Lina will follow up with an updated security pack. Lina, can you confirm the KMS/HSM contacts and audit log export?
[02:34] Lina: yep I'll pull the latest SOC2 attestation and we also have the KMS integration guide — will send both tonight.
[02:45] Samir: good. also, on the fallback side, we want a graceful degrade that uses a lower-capacity model with the same API contract; is that straightforward?
[02:58] Omar: yep, we have model variants that can be routed by policy; we can configure an automatic fallback to the small-quantized variant. question: are you ok with brief quality delta during the canary?
[03:12] Samir: yes as long as it's transparent to app teams and metrics are tracked.
[03:20] Evan: one issue we saw: when the queue backed up it hit connection limits on our LB and we had retries which amplified the problem. we need a short circuit at client or gateway so the queue doesn't self-amplify.
[03:35] Maya: that sounds like a backpressure control item — we can propose a client side throttling pattern and share rate-limiter configs.
[03:46] Priya: can you also include guidance for concurrent request caps per token-length distribution? we noticed longer sequences were the worst.
[03:58] Omar: yes, we'll run sample distributions against the patched runtime and recommend per-route concurrency caps.
[04:10] Samir: for the hotfix timeline — what can you deliver and when?
[04:18] Omar: target is to cut a hotfix branch today, run unit + integration tests tomorrow, and a staged canary next week. pragmatic dates: patch branch by 12/22, internal canary on 1/4, full rollout after success.
[04:32] Maya: we'll also provide a short changelog and compatibility notes for your deploy runbook.
[04:38] Evan: on logs — we will upload request traces to the shared bucket, but expect redaction noise for PII. will that be ok?
[04:47] Omar: yes we can work with redacted traces; the key things are trace ids, timing, and the KV miss patterns.
[04:55] Priya: about rollback — what safety nets do you suggest if the hotfix misbehaves?
[05:02] Omar: we propose a stepwise rollout with a canary percentage, health checks anchored on p95 latency and error rate and an automatic rollback if thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
[05:17] Samir: who owns the rollback trigger? ops or Redwood?
[05:22] Maya: operations should own the final trigger, but we can set the automation to recommend and optionally auto-trigger if you prefer.
[05:31] Priya: prefer manual to start, with automation ready to flip if we want in phase two.
[05:37] Lina: ok we'll document both options in the playbook.
[05:42] Evan: small ask — can you include a short mitigation for connection storms (short circuit and circuit breaker thresholds)?
[05:50] Omar: yes, that'll be in the runbook and we'll include recommended LB config.
[05:56] Samir: thanks. last thing: we need a short executive blurb for our internal postmortem to show customers; anything we should call out or avoid?
[06:07] Maya: call out the root cause (cache growth + eviction pathology), mitigation (hotfix and telemetry), timeline, and planned follow-ups (canary + new per-route caps). avoid specifics of internal kernel-level optimizations — keep it at platform level.
[06:22] Samir: got it.

-- Ambient cross-talk and filler: some people type in chat, "we're uploading logs", "on it", a couple of dropped words from the auto-transcript like "dedicate" vs "dedicated" and "kv cache" rendered as "k v cash".

Recap and agreed next steps (verbatim):
- Redwood: hotfix branch + changelog by 2026-12-22 (Omar)
- Crestline: upload traces and heap snapshots by 2026-12-23 (Evan)
- Redwood: security pack + SOC2 attestation link by 2026-12-21 (Lina)
- Crestline: internal canary signoff checklist by 2027-01-02 (Priya)

Action items (recorded separately above).

Questions raised during call:
- "Will rollback keep previous perf improvements?" answered: no, rollback reverts perf gains but stabilizes service quickly.
- "Do we have automatic fallback to quantized model?" answered: yes — routing policy supports variant fallback.
- "What telemetry is required?" answered: token-level traces, KV hit/miss counts, and heap/GC snapshots.

Meeting close and scheduling:
Maya: i'll send the meeting notes and the security doc tonight. let's reconvene after the hotfix is cut — aim for a 30 minute follow-up once traces are analyzed.
Samir: sounds good thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
